resource.name: Building and Safety Permit Information Old
resource.description: The Department of Building and Safety issues permits for the construction, remodeling, and repair of buildings and structures in the City of Los Angeles.  Permits are categorized into building permits, electrical permits, and mechanical permits (which include plumbing, HVAC systems, fire sprinklers, elevators, and pressure vessels).  Depending on the complexity of a project, a permit may be issued the same day with Express Permit or e-Permit ("No Plan Check" category), or a permit may require that the plans be reviewed ("Plan Check" category) by a Building and Safety Plan Check personnel.

The city and state of the permit applicant's address.
If applicable, permit applicant's business name.

The property/structure valuation amount is used to calculate the building permit fee and all fees calculated as percentage of the building fee.  For all building permit types, except for Grading, the valuation is measured in dollars. For Grading permit applications, the valuation is measured in cubic yards of soil removed or added.
Permit issue date.

This is the permit number assigned by the Plan Check and Inspection System as soon as an application for a permit has been filed.  Before a permit is issued, the number is known as the Application Number.  After the permit is issued, this same number becomes the Permit Number.
"Street address" portion of contractor's address.
Zip code of property address for permit application.

Ending unit number of property address on permit application. 
Example 1: For "200 - 200 N Main Ave, #1-#8", Unit Range End is #8. 
Example 2: For "202 1/4 - 204 1/2 N Main St SE", Unit Range End is null.

Beginning unit number of property address on permit application. 
Example 1: For "200 - 200 N Main Ave, #1-#8", Unit Range Start is #1. 
Example 2: For "202 1/4 - 204 1/2 N Main St SE", Unit Range Start is null.
Middle name of the contractor or personnel currently associated with the license.
First name of the contractor or personnel currently associated with the license.
Contractor's license number.
"City" portion of contractor's address.
"State" portion of contractor's address.

Street suffix direction of property address for permit application. Example 1: For "200 - 200 N Main Ave", Suffix Direction is null. 
Example 2: For "202 1/4 - 204 1/2 N Main St SE", Suffix Direction is SE.

Street suffix of property address for permit application. 
Example 1: For "200 - 200 Main Ave", Street Suffix is Ave. 
Example 2: For "202 1/4 - 204 1/2 N Main St SE", Street Suffix is St.
Office location where the permit application is initiated, not necessarily issued.
The City of Los Angeles council district that has jurisdiction over the property.

Street direction of property address for permit application.
Example 1: For "200 - 200 Main Ave", Street Direction is null. 
Example 2: For "202 1/4 - 204 1/2 N Main St SE", Street Direction is N.
An event code, usually synonymous with a disaster code, represents permits issued related to repairing, demolishing, or rebuilding structures damaged from a disaster.
Permit application type.
GPS location point.
A number used to associate a permit application with a specific construction or a development project consisting of several permit applications.
The permit sub-type determines whether the permit application is for a 1 or 2 family dwelling, a multi-family dwelling, or a commercial structure.
Describes the work to be performed under the permit application.
Floor area as defined in the Los Angeles Zoning Code.
Number of dwelling units for a residential building.
Number of accessory dwelling units for a residential building.
Number of stories.
If applicable, the contractor's business name.
Contractor's license type (class code).
First name of the permit applicant.
The unit portion of the permit applicant's address.
